ai.description: Duttaphrynus scaber is a small toad reaching 5 cm. It is yellowish-brown with dark spots and a distinct pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a warty skin and prominent, elongated parotoid glands.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus scaber* is best distinguished by its prominent, continuous cranial ridges that form a distinct "X" shape on the head, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Duttaphrynus scaber* inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: Schneider's toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects and other small invertebrates across its varied forest and grassland habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus scaber* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in long gelatinous strings in shallow water. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Duttaphrynus scaber is endemic to the Western Ghats and parts of peninsular India, typically inhabiting low to mid-elevation forests and agricultural landscapes.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus scaber* is a high-pitched, rapid series of metallic chirps, typically heard near temporary rain pools or streams in forested areas.
